offers.name: CDO as a Service
offers.one_line: A fractional Chief Data Officer for pharma manufacturers whose data is trapped in plant systems, spreadsheets and regulatory filings.
offers.who_for: Mid-size pharma / bulk-drug manufacturers, roughly 100-1000 staff, multiple plants or export markets, with an IT function but no data leadership.
offers.problem: Batch records, QC results, ERP and regulatory submissions all live in separate systems. Nobody owns the definition of a number, so every audit, every customer qualification and every management report is rebuilt by hand.
what_we_do: Data ownership model and a single definition layer across plant, quality and commercial systems
Regulatory and customer-audit reporting that assembles itself instead of being rebuilt
A roadmap the existing IT team can execute, with us accountable for the outcome
signals: More than one manufacturing site or unit listed
Exports, or US/EU regulatory approvals mentioned (FDA, EDQM, WHO-GMP, CEP, DMF)
Quality / compliance / accreditation pages with named certifications
Careers page hiring IT, MIS, ERP or QA roles but no data or analytics leadership
ERP named on the site (SAP, Oracle, Tally) without any analytics layer
disqualifiers: Single small unit, no exports, no named certifications
Trading or distribution only — no manufacturing of their own
Already advertises a data or analytics leadership function

offers.name: CAIO as a Service
offers.one_line: A fractional Chief AI Officer for manufacturers with an AI mandate from the board and nobody qualified to own it.
offers.who_for: Pharma manufacturers where leadership has committed to 'doing AI' but has no in-house AI capability and is being sold point tools by vendors.
offers.problem: AI arrives as disconnected vendor pilots — a chatbot here, a vision system there — none of them owned, measured or connected to a P&L line. Spend accumulates and nothing reaches production.
what_we_do: An AI portfolio tied to business outcomes, not tools, with a kill rule for each pilot
Vendor and build/buy decisions made by someone with no stake in the sale
Governance the regulator will accept: model provenance, validation, audit trail
signals: Public statements about digital transformation, Industry 4.0 or AI adoption
Recent funding, expansion or a new plant — budget and a change mandate
A named CIO/CTO/Head of Digital but no AI or data science leadership
Existing automation vendors visible on the site or in press coverage
disqualifiers: No digital signal anywhere on the site
Under ~100 staff — the mandate and the budget will not be there
Already has a named AI or data science leader

offers.name: AI Automations
offers.one_line: Automating the document and approval load that pharma manufacturing runs on — batch records, CoAs, dossiers, customer qualifications.
offers.who_for: Pharma manufacturers whose staff spend their days moving documents: QA, regulatory affairs, export documentation, customer qualification packs.
offers.problem: Every batch, every shipment and every customer qualification generates a pack of documents that a person assembles, checks and chases. It scales with volume, it does not scale with headcount, and mistakes are expensive.
what_we_do: Automated assembly and checking of batch records, CoAs and regulatory dossiers
Customer qualification and audit-response packs generated from existing systems
Human approval kept in the loop where the regulator requires it
signals: Wide product catalogue or many SKUs — document load scales with it
Export markets, which multiply documentation per shipment
Named certifications implying formal, documented quality processes
Careers page hiring regulatory affairs, documentation or QA coordinators
Downloadable CoAs, MSDS or product dossiers on the site
disqualifiers: Very small catalogue and domestic-only sales
No quality or regulatory function evident anywhere
